newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares push just ahead after jobless data.
newsitem.headline: German shares push just ahead after jobless data.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of leading shares on Thursday shrugged off overnight weakness on Wall Street to move into modest positive territory as the dollar strengthened after the publication of German jobless data.

The DAX-30 index rose 6.65 points to 3,104.65 in early bourse trade after the publication of higher-than-expected German jobless figures for January showing a climb of over half a million unemployed to 4.66 million.

Shares edged higher as the dollar pushed up to trade at 1.653 marks on the news. DAX futures, which had rallied in post-bourse trade on Wednesday, managed to shave some of their early Thursday losses to trade 9.0 points down at 3,113.0.
Dealers said the firmness of the dollar, together with continued strong demand for selected chemical stocks, would likely insulate the market against any significant losses during the day.
"We see it ending around (its current level of) 3,100 points," said one dealer.

Shares in engineering group Preussag rose 8.50 marks to 396.50 after it said it planned an unchanged dividend for 1995/96 of 12 marks. Dealers said there had been some fears in the market that it would announce a cut to 10 marks.
Engineering group Mannesmann rose 16 marks to 659.50 after Merrill Lynch raised the stock to a "buy" from "neutral" and, according to dealers, raised its target price for the stock significantly.
Software group SAP slipped 3.80 marks to 245.20 after a placement at 244 marks of some 3.54 million SAP shares once held by SAP's co-founder Hans-Werner Hector, who resigned in late 1996.
